newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM to study complaints on corporate tax.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM to study complaints on corporate tax.

text.p: Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda told Indian businessmen on Tuesday he would consider their complaints against a recently introduced minimum alternate tax (MAT) on corporations before next year's budget.

"About your point on taxation, we have taken note for consideration when next year's budget is being formulated," he told the 69th annual meeting of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).
The government is expected to present the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to parliament in late February.
Deve Gowda was responding to FICCI president Deepak Banker, who said the MAT had contributed to a slowdown in industrial and export growth.
